edition.name: Migne, Patrologia Latina (PL 2, Paris 1844), De resurrectione carnis, via Latin Wikisource transcription
edition.locus: On the Resurrection of the Flesh IX
edition.witness_note: Single locked witness in repo; second witness not yet locked.

source_text: Igitur, ut retexam quam Deus manibus suis ad imaginem Dei struxit, quam de suo adflatu ad similitudinem suae vivacitatis animavit, quam incolatui, fructui, dominatui, totius suae operationis praeposuit, quam sacramentis suis disciplinisque vestivit: cujus munditias amat, cujus castigationes probat, cujus passiones sibi adpretiat; haeccine non resurget totiens Dei? Absit, absit, ut Deus manuum suarum operam ingenii sui curam, adflatus sui vaginam, molitionis suae reginam, liberalitatis suae haeredem, religionis suae sacerdotem, testimonii sui militem, Christi sui sororem, in aeternum destituat interitum! Bonum Deum novimus; solum optimum a Christo ejus addiscimus; qui dilectionem mandans, post suam, in proximum, faciet et ipse quod praecepit: diliget carnem, tot modis sibi proximam, etsi infirmam; sed virtus in infirmitate perficitur; etsi imbecillam; sed medicum non desiderant, nisi male habentes; etsi inhonestam; sed inhonestioribus majorem circumdamus honorem; etsi perditam; sed ego, inquit, veni ut quod periit salvum faciam; etsi peccatricem; sed malo mihi, inquit, salutem peccatoris, quam mortem; etsi damnatam; sed ego, inquit, percutiam, et sanabo. Quid ea exprobras carni, quae Deum exspectant, quae in Deum sperant, quae honorantur ab illo, quibus subvenit? Ausim dicere, si haec carni non accidissent, benignitas, gratia, misericordia, omnis vis Dei benefica, vacuisset.
pass_a_gloss: Therefore, so that I may reexamine what God with His own hands built to the image of God, what from His own breath He animated to the likeness of His own vivacity, what He put in charge of dwelling, of fruit, of dominion, of all His operation, what He clothed with His own sacraments and disciplines: whose purity He loves, whose chastisements He approves, whose passions He esteems for Himself; will this not rise again, so often God's? Let it be absent, let it be absent, that God abandon to eternal destruction the work of His hands, the care of His intellect, the sheath of His breath, the queen of His molding, the heir of His liberality, the priest of His religion, the soldier of His testimony, the sister of His Christ! We know God is good; we learn from Christ that He is the only best; who, commanding love, after His own, to the neighbor, will also Himself do what He commanded: He will love the flesh, so many ways near to Him, even if weak; but virtue is perfected in weakness; even if feeble; but those who are well do not need a physician; even if dishonorable; but we surround with greater honor those more dishonorable; even if lost; but I, He says, came that what was lost I may save; even if sinful; but it is worse for Me, He says, the death of the sinner than salvation; even if condemned; but I, He says, will strike and I will heal. What do you reproach this flesh for, which await God, which hope in God, which are honored by Him, to which He brings help? I dare to say, if these things had not happened to the flesh, the kindness, the grace, the mercy, all the beneficial power of God would have been empty.

bible_refs.note: I came to seek and to save the lost
those who are well do not need a physician
it is not the will of your Father who is in heaven that one of these little ones should perish

pass_b_english: So let me reexamine what God built with His own hands in the image of God, what He animated with His own breath to the likeness of His own vivacity, what He placed in charge of dwelling, fruit, dominion, and all His work, what He clothed with His own sacraments and disciplines — whose purity He loves, whose chastisements He approves, whose passions He esteems for Himself. Will this not rise again, so often God's? God forbid, God forbid, that He should abandon to eternal destruction the work of His hands, the care of His intellect, the sheath of His breath, the queen of His molding, the heir of His liberality, the priest of His religion, the soldier of His testimony, the sister of His Christ! We know God is good; we learn from Christ that He is the only Best. Christ, who commanded love — after His own — for the neighbor, will Himself do what He commanded: He will love the flesh, so many ways near to Him, even if weak; but virtue is perfected in weakness (2 Cor 12:9). Even if feeble; but those who are well do not need a physician (Matt 9:12-13). Even if dishonorable; but we surround the more dishonorable with greater honor (1 Cor 12:23-24). Even if lost; but I came to save what was lost, He says (Luke 19:10). Even if sinful; but I desire the sinner's salvation, not death, He says (Ezek 33:11). Even if condemned; but I will strike and I will heal, He says (Hos 6:1). What do you reproach this flesh for, which awaits God, which hopes in God, which is honored by Him, to which He brings help? I dare say: if these things had not happened to the flesh, the kindness, the grace, the mercy, all the beneficial power of God would have been empty.

anf_compare.notes: Drafted from source only; ANF not shown to drafter.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the Latin text. Pass B correctly identifies and adds the necessary scripture citations for the various allusions (2 Cor 12:9, Matt 9:12-13, 1 Cor 12:23-24, Luke 19:10, Ezek 33:11, Hos 6:1) which were present in the sense of the Latin but not explicitly cited in the source text, fulfilling the requirement for added identifications. Pass A and B are consistent in meaning.
